note: hecks_qa SW-roster-1789342760 (seed 5, shrunk 25 -> 2 steps) — Roster::Roster.Mark declares its own fact literally named `to` (BUG#7/#16/#17/#18's own famous collision with the routing envelope's reserved `to` key), and a `dry_run` step built from the fuzzer's flat legacy-args convention (`{"dry_run": verb, "args": {"to": ..., "name": ...}}`, never a step-level `to`/`with` envelope) carries that fact as `args["to"]`. Ruby's `Dispatcher#dry_run?(verb, **args)` has NO `to:`/`with:` keyword parameters at all (unlike `#dispatch`, which does and routes through `Routing.envelope`/`Routing.payload`) — every key of `args`, `to` included, is forwarded straight through as flat command facts, uninterpreted, so a real, non-null `to` fact dry-runs cleanly (`ok: true`). Rust's `dry_run()` (kernel/cli.rs) shares its `command_input`/`CommandInvocation::from_json` parsing with REAL dispatch, which does not: `to` present and non-null unconditionally selects the explicit-routing branch (`non_null_to_still_takes_the_routing_branch_not_the_legacy_one`, kernel/routing.rs, pins this for `from_json` in isolation) — so Mark's own `to` fact, wrapped `{"value": 570}` by the value-object coercion, is parsed as a routing-envelope Hash, found to have no `"aggregate"` key, and refused `TypeMismatch("entity route requires a scalar aggregate identity")` before the domain's own `MarkArgs::from_json` (which correctly permits `to` alongside the identity field `name`, `unknown_keys(["to", "id", "roster", "name"])`) is ever reached. Ruby: ok: true. Rust: ok: false. The fix belongs in `command_input()`'s own dry-run call sites, not in the shared `CommandInvocation::from_json`/`RoutingEnvelope` used by real dispatch (whose own to/with-sniffing behavior real dispatch legitimately relies on and a pinned unit test protects) — dry-run's own command_input must never be to/with-sniffed at all, matching Ruby's `dry_run?` signature exactly.
